poo_customs_off.text: The Custom House is where cargoes were measured, taxed and sometimes argued over. In 1747 a gang broke into the previous building to get back a cargo of tea that officers had seized from a smuggler.

Tea was heavily taxed, so smugglers brought it in cheap from the Continent. A great deal of the Channel Islands' history is about boats coming and going with something under the nets. Mostly lace and brandy.
